healthcareSystem: British Overseas Territory with a well-equipped hospital and private clinics. King Edward VII Memorial Hospital is the main facility. Healthcare is expensive — similar to US pricing.
qualityNotes: King Edward VII Memorial Hospital provides good general and emergency care with modern equipment. Several specialist services available on-island. For complex procedures, patients are evacuated to the US (Boston or Baltimore). Private clinics offer high-quality care for routine needs.
pharmacyHours: Pharmacies open 8am-6pm weekdays, 9am-5pm Saturday. Hospital pharmacy available for emergencies.
pharmacyTips: Several pharmacies across the island are well-stocked. US and UK brands common. Prices are higher than the US mainland. Staff speak English.
prescriptionRules: Prescription required for most medications. US and UK prescriptions generally recognized. Good stock of common medications.

restrictedMeds.name: Cannabis/CBD products
restrictedMeds.note: Illegal in Bermuda. Do not bring any cannabis products.

restrictedMeds.name: Controlled substances
restrictedMeds.note: Carry a doctor's letter, prescription, and keep in original packaging. Declare at customs.

bringDocumentation: Carry prescriptions and a doctor's letter for all medications. English documentation is standard. Keep medications in original labeled containers. Bermuda customs may inspect medications.

travelInsurance.tips: Healthcare in Bermuda is VERY expensive — similar to US pricing. Medical evacuation to the US can cost $20,000-50,000+. Ensure coverage includes water sports, scooter accidents (very common), and medical evacuation.

vaccinations.notes: No special vaccinations required. Bermuda has no tropical disease risks. Standard health precautions apply.

waterNotes: Tap water is safe to drink. Bermuda collects rainwater on white limestone roofs — this is the primary water source and is well-filtered. Bottled water also available.
foodSafetyTips: Excellent food safety standards throughout the island. Restaurants are well-regulated. Fresh fish (especially wahoo and rockfish) is a highlight. Bermuda has strict food safety inspections.
medicalTourismNote: Bermuda is not a medical tourism destination due to high costs. Residents needing specialist care travel to the US, primarily Boston or Baltimore.
sources: Government of Bermuda — Department of Health
metaDescription: Health guide for Bermuda. King Edward VII Hospital, pharmacy access, scooter safety tips, high medical costs, and evacuation insurance advice.

hospitals.name: King Edward VII Memorial Hospital
hospitals.notes: Main hospital with 24/7 emergency department. Modern facility with CT, MRI, and surgical capabilities. Only acute care hospital on the island.

hospitals.name: Mid-Atlantic Wellness Institute
hospitals.notes: Psychiatric and substance abuse facility. Not for general emergencies.

hospitals.name: Bermuda General Hospital
hospitals.notes: Government facility. Limited English. Bring a translator app.

dentalCare.availability: Several private dental practices with modern equipment and well-trained dentists.
dentalCare.costRange: $100-350 USD for basic procedures — comparable to US pricing
dentalCare.notes: Good quality dental care but expensive. Many dentists trained in the US, UK, or Canada.
dentalCare.emergencyTip: Call King Edward VII Memorial Hospital for after-hours dental emergencies, or contact a private dentist directly.

mentalHealth.internationalLine: Crisis Text Line: text HELLO to 741741 (US-based)
mentalHealth.englishTherapists: Several English-speaking therapists and counselors available in private practice.
mentalHealth.notes: Mental health services are available but limited compared to larger countries. Mid-Atlantic Wellness Institute is the primary facility.

accessibilityInfo.overview: Bermuda has made improvements in accessibility but the historic architecture and narrow roads present challenges.
accessibilityInfo.hospitalAccess: King Edward VII Memorial Hospital is fully wheelchair accessible.
accessibilityInfo.transport: Public buses have limited accessibility. Ferries have some wheelchair access. Taxis can accommodate some needs.
accessibilityInfo.tips: Many hotels and resorts have accessible rooms — book in advance. Historic sites may have limited access. Sidewalks can be narrow and uneven.

covidStatus.entryRequirements: No COVID testing or vaccination requirements for entry as of 2026.
covidStatus.maskPolicy: No mask mandates. May be requested in healthcare settings.
covidStatus.testing: Testing available at King Edward VII Memorial Hospital and private labs.
covidStatus.notes: Bermuda has returned to normal operations. Standard precautions apply.

insuranceClaimProcess: King Edward VII Memorial Hospital accepts major credit cards and insurance. Non-residents should expect to pay upfront or provide insurance details. Obtain itemized bills with diagnosis codes. US insurance may provide partial coverage — check before traveling.

commonCosts.note: Healthcare costs are HIGH — comparable to the US. USD accepted everywhere at par. Travel insurance strongly recommended.

medicalEvacuation.primaryDestination: Boston, USA (Massachusetts General Hospital / Brigham and Women's)
medicalEvacuation.note: Air ambulance to the US East Coast takes about 2 hours. Bermuda Hospitals Board coordinates evacuations. Multiple daily commercial flights to the US also available.

pharmacyChains.name: Clarien Pharmacy (at KEMH)
pharmacyChains.where: King Edward VII Memorial Hospital, Paget

drugNameMap.note: Widely available OTC at all pharmacies.
